sec: Renal failure flowchart & RPRF causes · p778

items.q: Complete the classification flowchart of renal failure — 1) CKD  2) Non-CKD presenting over hours–days  3) Non-CKD presenting over days–weeks … A) Acute kidney injury (AKI)  B) Rapidly progressive renal failure (RPRF)  C) Chronic kidney disease
items.exp: Flowchart: renal failure splits into CKD and non-CKD; non-CKD presenting over hours–days is AKI, and over days–weeks is rapidly progressive renal failure. (Book p778)

items.q: Rapidly progressive renal failure (RPRF) is defined in the flowchart by a presentation over:
items.exp: The flowchart timings: AKI = hours to days; RPRF = days to weeks. (Book p778)

items.q: Match each cause with its place in the flowchart — 1) Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis  2) Hemolytic uremic syndrome  3) Severe acute interstitial nephritis  4) Atheroembolic renal disease … A) Causes of RPRF, some cases being atheroembolic
opts: All four are listed causes of RPRF
Only 1 and 2 are causes of RPRF
Only 3 is a cause of RPRF
All four are causes of AKI, not RPRF
items.exp: Causes of RPRF listed under the flowchart: RPGN (due to glomerular pathology), hemolytic uremic syndrome, severe acute interstitial nephritis (AIN), and atheroembolic renal disease (some cases). (Book p778)

items.q: Which of these is NOT listed as a cause of rapidly progressive renal failure?
items.exp: ATN is the classic cause of AKI (hours–days), not of RPRF; RPRF causes listed are RPGN, HUS, severe AIN and atheroembolic renal disease. (Book p778)

items.q: The flowchart attributes rapidly progressive renal failure chiefly to glomerular pathology.
opts: True — RPGN is listed first among RPRF causes and is due to glomerular pathology
False — RPRF is due to tubular pathology
True — it is due entirely to interstitial pathology
False — RPRF is defined by vascular pathology only
items.exp: Under RPRF the first listed cause is rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN), annotated 'due to glomerular pathology'. (Book p778)

items.q: RPGN is defined as RPRF plus:
opts: Diffuse proliferative glomerulonephritis with crescents on light microscopy
Diffuse mesangial IgA deposition with normal light microscopy
Acute tubular necrosis with muddy brown casts
items.exp: RPGN = RPRF + diffuse proliferative glomerulonephritis with crescents (an HPE/light-microscopy feature). (Book p778)
